via.name: Mistletoe Bay

evidence: You can walk or ride the track in either direction, but it's best to start from Meretoto/Ship Cove.
There is no road to Meretoto/Ship Cove so you will need to arrange boat transport to start your walk there.
The final hour's walking is on an easy path through mature beech forest to Anakiwa.
At Anakiwa are a carpark, shelter, toilets and phone near the track end, and a public jetty opposite the Outward Bound school.

side_trips.quote: At Meretoto/Ship Cove, you can take the Waterfall Track to a small waterfall in the forest (40 min return).

doubts: The page says the track can be walked in either direction but is best started from Meretoto/Ship Cove, so the main way runs Ship Cove to Anakiwa. The Ship Cove start has no road end (boat access); ref is the Meretoto / Ship Cove coast entry. The head of Endeavour Inlet was given the Endeavour Inlet coast entry (T14); the place entry T13 lies elsewhere, and for the sea access point I left the ref null since it is unclear which is meant. Torea Saddle is given as F1 (where the Queen Charlotte Track meets Torea Road) as the road crossing at the saddle. Te Mahia Saddle and Mistletoe Saddle may be the Onahau Road crossings (F6/F7) but the text does not tie them, so null. Cowshed Bay Campsite is one of the six DOC campsites 'on the track' but the text does not say the track passes it. A direct track bypassing Camp Bay to Kenepuru Saddle is mentioned as an alternative; not recorded as a way. Mountain-biking options and Kenepuru Road are bike alternatives, not recorded. James Vogel Nature Track is spelled 'Nature Walk' on the map (T2).
